newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac's political musical chairs at Rugby meet.
newsitem.headline: Chirac's political musical chairs at Rugby meet.

text.p: It may be body language or it may not, but French President Jacques Chirac is to sit in full view of millions of television viewers on Saturday close to the two men seen as best placed to become his next premier.

Sharing the VIP stand with the conservative Chirac at the French Rugby Union championship final in Paris on the eve of Sunday's crucial parliamentary election runoff will be fellow Gaullist Philippe Seguin and Socialist Party chief Lionel Jospin.
Chirac's office said he had invited Seguin, speaker of the outgoing National Assembly, to be his guest at the match.

Seguin, on cool terms with the president since being passed over for premier two years ago, is widely touted by media as the man Chirac will name as government chief if the centre-right wins the election.
But Socialist Jospin will also be in the official stand because one of the two teams in the final, Stade Toulousain, is based close to his southwest France constituency.
Chirac's office confirmed press reports that Jospin had called them about seating, requesting that he not be placed near scandal-tarnished Paris mayor Jean Tiberi, a former Chirac aide.

According to the tentative seating plan, all three men are in the front row of the VIP box with Seguin directly to Chirac's right. Tiberi will be two seats away in his capacity as mayor and Jospin two seats further removed, informed sources said.
Jospin is in line to become prime minister if the left wins the election, inaugurating an uneasy period of joint rule, or "cohabitation," with the president.

Chirac has not publicly said whom he favours to replace Alain Juppe, sacked after the centre-right's poor performance in last Sunday's first round of voting. But Seguin is widely believed to be in line for the post.
Playing against Stade Toulousain is Bourgouin-Jallieu from central France.
Oddly, Chirac and Jospin sat on either side of the late President Francois Mitterrand two years ago at the same championship event on the eve of Chirac's election over Jospin to replace Mitterrand.
